newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fernz to sell NZ fertiliser businesses.
newsitem.headline: Fernz to sell NZ fertiliser businesses.

text.p: Fernz Corp Ltd said on Wednesday that it was completing legal agreements involving the sale of its fertiliser manufacturing businesses in New Zealand.
The transactions would generate NZ$105 million, which Fernz planned to invest in continued growth and development of its international agricultural chemicals operations.

"The New Zealand domestic fertiliser market is mature and the company believes that growth prospects for its other business sectors provide greater opportunity for shareholder value creation in the future," Fernz said in a statement.
Fernz said the New Plymouth operation would be sold to Ravensdown Fertiliser Co-op.
Revensdown plans to stop manufacture at New Plymouth but continue to import high analysis products and additives through that port.
Superphosphate required in the region would be made at Ravensdown's Napier plant and blended and dispatched from the New Plymouth Works for farmer clients.
The Whangarei plant would be be sold to Bay of Plenty Fertiliser and its operations would continue.
Fernz planned to retain its 40 percent interest in BOP Fertiliser, including the Mt Maunganui and Whangarei Works and Petrochem.
Both transactions were to become effective on June 1.
Fernz last traded at NZ$4.70, down two cents.
